i have the desire to start a biotech company. why? 
1) i have the intuition that academia is not the right culture for me. why? With the caveat that I have a small sample size, my experience in academia has been that people are not working on ambitious projects.  What I have found in industries is that people are working on ambitious projects projects. this is what i want. For whatever reason, perhaps due to outstanding academic culture or funding incentives or idrc and it doesn't matter as much as the fact of the matter. I'm open to having my mind changed on the culture of academia. 
1a) why is culture important? i think it really shapes what you want (mimetic desire) (im not gonna larp and say ive read any René Girard but i get the idea) . Anecdotally, i go to cornell, and i see how this plays out with the kinds of careers that people want. I don't feel like over explaining myself in this sense but what i will say is that i dont want what people in academia typically want. I don't want to adopt the desires. I do want to adopt the desires of ambitious entrepreneurs, though. 

2) I care about a tangible product rather than the creation of knowledge itself (another reason why academia is not right for me). why? It feels less self-serving and ultimately, will I lie on my deathbed I think I will be happier having created a product that I feel impacted humanity in a positive way rather than strictly pursuing my own curiosity like what academia does. lmao i didnt mean to shit all over academia in this post it more about pinning down to myself why does it feel right for me. 

3) so then why biotech as opposed to anything else? I have done some thinking about this, and what I have told myself is that okay, let's start from the beginning: From when I was a kid, my mom encourage me to be a doctor, but not in the sense that you must do this and it's in order. It's more like it would be cool if you did this in the most loving way possible. I kind of adopted that, and it predisposed me to liking biology, and so then I grew a genuine love for biology and then that has branched out, as I got older, into the STEM fields as a whole, but still biology on top. and since ive tested higher in math/science from a younger age, ((but as early as i can remember, this was reinforced when in 7th grade when i got a nwea score in 7th grade science of like 232 ( 90th to 95th percentile on a quick google search) and i remember my 7th grade science teacher pulling me to the side and was like yo youre onto something here. i also )) its just been self reinforcing that like biology is for me and I think this is about as fundamental as it gets and like i think this is a good place to start for intrinsic motivation but then thinking about how to serve humanity with that is what I think will lead to
